Yes, the 2025 clearing of this native forest on the property appears to be illegal under Uruguayan law.

The tool output shows that 13.1 hectares of native forest were cleared in 2025. According to Uruguay’s 2009 Forest Law, native forest clearing is prohibited, with strict controls on any exceptions. The evidence confirms the area was indeed native forest (not planted), and the clearing was not authorized in the MGAP’s 2021 forest inventory. Additionally, the event meets the corroboration criteria (JRC 2020 confirms 98% of the area was forest in 2020). Since no legal exemptions are recorded, this clearing violates Uruguayan environmental regulations.
